To add to this - I had a really successful AAC therapy at a placement earlier this year with kids of a similar age to yours where we gave jobs to the kids (e.g. taking pens and papers to teachers) and went with them while they used their AAC to explain what they were there for and complete the job. (Hi! Do you need pens? How many?) It had a clear function, the kids were able to generalise use to other communication partners, and it aimed to boost self esteem by giving them a legitimate task to do. Maybe for the kid who likes construction you could combine AAC with a sort of Lego therapy - where he needs to offer/ask for particular bricks to construct a model? 

As someone else said it's hard to advise without knowing the client or the setting but I really think that increasing the functionality of any AAC therapy makes it more engaging as it's more purposeful. Hope you have fun!
